decisions.reason: "Wivu" is jealousy, and "bidii" is mere hard work. "Ari" is fervent devotion, the sense of the Greek word (m4); Readable says "hamu kubwa" (strong eagerness).

decisions.choice: passé composé for the events of Paul's own account (1:13-2:14) at every level, with the imparfait for what went on over a time ("je persécutais", "elles entendaient")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je montai à Jérusalem")
decisions.reason: The French style guide puts written narrative in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced. Here, though, the narrative is Paul's own story told in the first person to the readers of a letter ("vous avez entendu"), and modern French tells such a story in the passé composé, as Colossians and the arguments of Hebrews do. A first-person passé simple ("je montai", "je lui résistai") would sound literary and distant. A reviewer may prefer the passé simple at Balanced.

decisions.choice: je la dévastais (L); je m'acharnais à la détruire (B); j'essayais de la faire disparaître (R)
decisions.reason: The verb was used of sacking a city, and its imperfect shows an attempt that did not succeed (m2). Literal keeps the picture with "dévaster"; Balanced and Readable make the attempt plain.

decisions.choice: "교회" for the church at every level, here and through the letter
decisions.reason: "교회" is the ordinary Korean word for God's people gathered in Christ, both a local congregation (1:2, 1:22) and the whole church Paul attacked (the meaning decision), and it is plain enough for Readable. The same word is used in Colossians and Romans.

decisions.choice: Balanced moves the reason (his zeal for the traditions) before the main clause within verse 14
alternatives: the Greek order, with the zeal last
decisions.reason: Korean puts a reason before what it explains. Both clauses belong to verse 14, so the verse keeps all its content after its marker.

decisions.choice: "đạo Do Thái" for Judaism
decisions.reason: The word is the Jewish way of life kept in loyalty to the law (m1). "Đạo Do Thái" is the everyday Vietnamese name and covers a way of life as well as a religion; "Do Thái giáo" is a learned word. Readable adds that it is the Jewish way of life, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "nhiệt thành" (L, B); "hăng hái" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is fierce devotion (m4). "Nhiệt thành" is warm and strong devotion without the sense of a fanatic in "cuồng nhiệt".

source.text: ὅτε δὲ εὐδόκησεν ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εὐθέως οὐ προσανεθέμην σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι, οὐδὲ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ ἀποστόλους, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθον εἰς Ἀραβίαν, καὶ πάλιν ὑπέστρεψα εἰς Δαμασκόν.

records.literal_gloss: When but was pleased the [one] having set-apart me from [the] womb of mother of me and having called through the grace of him \v 16 to reveal the son of him in me so that I might preach him among the nations, immediately not I consulted with flesh and blood, \v 17 nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the before me apostles, but I went away into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.

en.L: But when the one who set me apart from my mother's womb and called [me] through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace was pleased \v 16 to reveal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son in me, so that I might preach {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the Gentiles, immediately I did not consult with flesh and blood, \v 17 nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those [who were] apostles before me, but I went away into Arabia, and again I returned to Damascus.
en.B: But God set me apart from birth and called me by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose \v 16 to reveal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son in me so that I would proclaim the gospel about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among the Gentiles, I did not at once turn to any human being for advice. \v 17 I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead I went away to Arabia, and afterward I came back to Damascus.
en.R: But even before I was born, God set me apart. Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called me. Then the time came when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was pleased \v 16 to show me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, so that I would tell the good news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to people who are not Jews. When that happened, I did not go to any person for advice. \v 17 I did not go up to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went off to Arabia. Later I went back to the city of Damascus.

es.L: Pero cuando el que me apartó desde el vientre de mi madre y [me] llamó por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia tuvo a bien \v 16 revelar a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo en mí, para que yo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} anunciara entre los gentiles, en seguida no consulté con carne y sangre, \v 17 ni subí a Jerusalén a los que eran apóstoles antes que yo, sino que me fui a Arabia, y volví de nuevo a Damasco.
es.B: Pero Dios me apartó desde mi nacimiento y me llamó por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, y cuando quiso \v 16 revelar a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo en mí para que yo anunciara el evangelio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entre los gentiles, no acudí enseguida a ningún ser humano en busca de consejo. \v 17 No subí a Jerusalén para ver a los que eran apóstoles antes que yo. Más bien me fui a Arabia, y después regresé a Damasco.
es.R: Pero aun antes de que yo naciera, Dios me apartó. Por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gracia, me llamó. Luego llegó el momento en que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agradó \v 16 mostrarme a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, para que yo anunciara la buena noticia acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a los que no son judíos. Cuando eso sucedió, no fui a pedir consejo a nadie. \v 17 No subí a Jerusalén para ver a los que eran apóstoles antes que yo. Más bien, me fui a Arabia. Más tarde volví a la ciudad de Damasco.

sw.L: Lakini ilipompendeza yule aliyenitenga tangu tumboni mwa mama yangu na kuniita kupitia neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} \v 16 kumfunua Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ndani yangu, ili nimhubiri kati ya watu wa mataifa, mara moja sikushauriana na mwili na damu, \v 17 wala sikupanda kwenda Yerusalemu kwa wale waliokuwa mitume kabla yangu, bali nilienda zangu Uarabuni, kisha nikarudi tena Dameski.
sw.B: Lakini Mungu alinitenga tangu kuzaliwa kwangu, akaniita kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na alipoamua \v 16 kumfunua Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ndani yangu ili nitangaze Injili inayomhusu kati ya watu wa mataifa, sikwenda mara moja kwa mwanadamu yeyote kutafuta ushauri. \v 17 Sikupanda kwenda Yerusalemu kuwaona wale waliokuwa mitume kabla yangu. Badala yake nilienda Uarabuni, na baadaye nikarudi Dameski.
sw.R: Lakini hata kabla sijazaliwa, Mungu alikuwa amenitenga. Kwa sababu ya neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, aliniita. Kisha wakati ukafika ambapo alipendezwa \v 16 kunionyesha Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ili niwaambie watu wasio Wayahudi Habari Njema inayomhusu. Jambo hilo lilipotokea, sikwenda kwa mtu yeyote kuomba ushauri. \v 17 Sikupanda kwenda Yerusalemu kuwaona wale waliokuwa mitume kabla yangu. Badala yake, nilienda Uarabuni. Baadaye nilirudi katika mji wa Dameski.

fr.L: Mais quand celui qui m’a mis à part dès le sein de ma mère et m’a appelé par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce a jugé bon \v 16 de révéler {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils en moi, afin que je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}annonce parmi les nations, aussitôt je n’ai consulté ni la chair ni le sang, \v 17 et je ne suis pas monté à Jérusalem vers ceux qui étaient apôtres avant moi, mais je suis parti en Arabie, puis je suis revenu à Damas.
fr.B: Mais Dieu m’avait mis à part dès ma naissance et m’avait appelé par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a jugé bon \v 16 de révéler {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils en moi, pour que j’annonce parmi les nations l’Évangile qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} concerne, je ne suis pas allé aussitôt demander conseil à qui que ce soit. \v 17 Je ne suis pas monté à Jérusalem pour voir ceux qui étaient apôtres avant moi. Je suis parti, au contraire, en Arabie, puis je suis revenu à Damas.
fr.R: Mais avant même ma naissance, Dieu m’avait mis à part. Par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a appelé. Puis le moment est venu où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a voulu \v 16 me montrer {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, pour que j’annonce la bonne nouvelle à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet aux peuples qui ne sont pas juifs. Quand c’est arrivé, je ne suis allé demander conseil à personne. \v 17 Je ne suis pas monté à Jérusalem pour voir ceux qui étaient apôtres avant moi. Je suis parti en Arabie. Plus tard, je suis retourné dans la ville de Damas.

ko.L: 그러나 나를 어머니의 태에서부터 따로 세우시고 그분의 은혜를 통하여 [나를] 부르신 분께서 \v 16 그분의 아들을 내 안에 나타내시기를 기뻐하셔서, 내가 그분을 이방 사람들 가운데 전하게 하셨을 때, 나는 곧바로 혈육과 의논하지 않았고, \v 17 나보다 먼저 사도가 된 사람들을 [만나러] 예루살렘으로 올라가지도 않았으며, 아라비아로 갔다가 다시 다메섹으로 돌아왔습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 하나님께서는 내가 태어나기 전부터 나를 따로 세우시고 그분의 은혜로 나를 부르셨습니다. 그리고 그분이 기뻐하시는 때에 \v 16 그분의 아들을 내 안에 나타내셔서, 내가 이방 사람들 가운데 그 아들에 관한 복음을 전하게 하셨습니다. 그때 나는 곧바로 어떤 사람과도 의논하지 않았고, \v 17 나보다 먼저 사도가 된 사람들을 만나러 예루살렘으로 올라가지도 않았습니다. 오히려 나는 아라비아로 갔다가, 그 뒤에 다메섹으로 돌아왔습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 하나님께서는 내가 태어나기도 전에 나를 따로 세우셨습니다. 하나님께서는 그분의 은혜로 나를 부르셨습니다. 그리고 하나님께서 기뻐하시는 때가 되자, \v 16 그분의 아들을 나에게 보여 주셨습니다. 내가 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 그 아들에 관한 기쁜 소식을 전하게 하시려는 것이었습니다. 그런 일이 있었을 때, 나는 어떤 사람에게도 의논하러 가지 않았습니다. \v 17 나보다 먼저 사도가 된 사람들을 만나러 예루살렘으로 올라가지도 않았습니다. 그 대신 아라비아로 떠났습니다. 그 뒤에 다메섹이라는 도시로 돌아갔습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng khi Đấng đã biệt riêng tôi từ trong lòng mẹ và đã gọi [tôi] bởi ân điển {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vui lòng \v 16 bày tỏ Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong tôi, để tôi rao giảng Tin Lành về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} giữa các dân ngoại, thì lập tức tôi không bàn hỏi với xác thịt và huyết, \v 17 cũng không lên Giê-ru-sa-lem gặp những người đã làm sứ đồ trước tôi, nhưng tôi đã đi qua A-ra-bi, rồi lại trở về Đa-mách.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã biệt riêng tôi từ khi tôi còn trong lòng mẹ, và đã gọi tôi bởi ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vui lòng \v 16 bày tỏ Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong tôi để tôi rao giảng Tin Lành về Con ấy giữa các dân ngoại, thì tôi không vội đi hỏi ý kiến một người nào. \v 17 Tôi cũng không lên Giê-ru-sa-lem gặp những người đã làm sứ đồ trước tôi. Trái lại, tôi đã đi qua A-ra-bi, rồi sau đó trở về Đa-mách.
vi.R: Nhưng ngay cả trước khi tôi sinh ra, Đức Chúa Trời đã biệt riêng tôi. Vì ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã gọi tôi. Rồi đến lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vui lòng \v 16 cho tôi biết Con của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để tôi nói Tin Lành về Con ấy cho những người không phải là người Do Thái. Khi điều đó xảy ra, tôi đã không đi hỏi ý kiến một người nào. \v 17 Tôi cũng không lên Giê-ru-sa-lem gặp những người đã làm sứ đồ trước tôi. Thay vào đó, tôi đi qua miền A-ra-bi. Sau đó tôi trở về thành Đa-mách.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the one who set me apart", without the word "God"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "God" after εὐδόκησεν; some important early ones do not, and SBLGNT follows them. A copyist was more likely to add the name than to drop it. The meaning is the same: the one who set Paul apart is God.

decisions.choice: set apart from his mother's womb and called: Paul's call is told in words used of the prophets
decisions.reason: The wording recalls Jeremiah 1:5 ("before you came out of the womb I set you apart ... a prophet to the nations") and Isaiah 49:1-6 (the servant called from the womb to be a light to the nations). Like them, Paul was chosen before birth and sent to the nations.

decisions.choice: in me: God revealed his Son to Paul, within him, so that Paul came to know him
alternatives: through me (God showed his Son to others through Paul's life)
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐμοὶ most naturally means God's inward revealing of Christ to Paul, the same event as "a revelation of Jesus Christ" in verse 12. It could also mean God revealed Christ through Paul to others, which the purpose clause ("so that I might preach him") would suit.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: the non-Jewish peoples
decisions.reason: ἔθνος in the plural is Paul's word for the peoples other than Israel (2:7-9).

decisions.choice: flesh and blood: any human being
decisions.reason: σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι is a Jewish expression for human beings in their weakness compared with God (Matthew 16:17). εὐθέως ("immediately") goes with the whole sentence: Paul's first move was not to consult anyone, but to go to Arabia.

decisions.choice: Arabia: the Nabatean kingdom to the south and east of Damascus; Damascus: the city where Paul first met the risen Christ
decisions.reason: Paul does not say what he did in Arabia. "Returned to Damascus" shows he had been there before going; Acts 9:1-22 places his conversion near the city.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting for God and his Son.

decisions.choice: God
alternatives: the one who set me apart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God, whom the phrase means (m1).

decisions.choice: from birth (B); even before I was born (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means from the start of his life; Readable follows Jeremiah 1:5, which it recalls (m2).

decisions.choice: I did not at once turn to any human being for advice (B); I did not go to any person for advice (R)
alternatives: I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood
decisions.reason: "Flesh and blood" is kept at Literal; the other levels say what it means (m5).

decisions.choice: proclaim the gospel about him (B); tell the good news about him (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "proclaim as good news"; Balanced and Readable say what Paul proclaims.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Gentiles" (m4).

decisions.choice: tuvo a bien
decisions.reason: "Le agradó al que me apartó" would put an unmarked pronoun for God before its noun; "tuvo a bien" says "was pleased" with the subject named, and keeps the verse break where the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: les nations (L, B); les peuples qui ne sont pas juifs, les non-Juifs (R) (for the whole letter); non-Juif where one person or a way of life is meant (2:12-15)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:27: "les Gentils" is no longer current French, and "les païens" now suggests people without religion or a judgment on them. "Les nations" keeps the biblical sense of the peoples other than Israel (m4); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: Quand il a jugé bon (B)
decisions.reason: The verb says that God was pleased to act; "juger bon" keeps that it was his free choice.

decisions.choice: "이방 사람들" (L, B); "유대인이 아닌 사람들" (R), through the letter
decisions.reason: As in Romans: "이방 사람" is the established word for a non-Jew and is still understood; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "혈육" (L); "어떤 사람" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Flesh and blood" means any human being (the meaning decision). Korean "혈육" (blood and flesh) is an existing word close to the Greek picture; it most often means one's own kin, so Balanced and Readable say plainly "any person", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "다메섹", "아라비아", "예루살렘"
decisions.reason: Place names follow the established Protestant Korean forms (docs/korean-style.md section 5).

decisions.choice: "các dân ngoại" (L, B); "những người không phải là người Do Thái" (R) for the Gentiles (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Dân ngoại" is the established word for the peoples other than Israel (m4), as in the Vietnamese Colossians and Romans; Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Tin Lành về Ngài" (L), "Tin Lành về Con ấy" (B, R) for "preach him"
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "proclaim the gospel", with "him" as its content. Vietnamese "rao giảng Ngài" is awkward, so "Tin Lành về" is said; Balanced and Readable name the Son, since "Ngài" in this sentence also stands for God.

decisions.choice: "xác thịt và huyết" (L); "một người nào" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew way of saying "a human being" (m5) with "xác thịt", the word kept for sarx, and "huyết"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: Ἔπειτα μετὰ ἔτη τρία ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἱστορῆσαι Κηφᾶν, καὶ ἐπέμεινα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας δεκαπέντε·

records.literal_gloss: Then after years three I went up to Jerusalem to get-to-know Cephas, and I remained with him days fifteen;

en.L: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Cephas, and I remained with him fifteen days.
en.B: Three years later I did go up to Jerusalem, to get to know Cephas, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.
en.R: Three years after that, I did go up to Jerusalem. I went to get to know Peter, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.

es.L: Después, al cabo de tres años, subí a Jerusalén para conocer a Cefas, y me quedé con él quince días.
es.B: Tres años más tarde sí subí a Jerusalén, para conocer a Cefas, y estuve con él quince días.
es.R: Tres años después, sí subí a Jerusalén. Fui para conocer a Pedro, y me quedé con él quince días.

sw.L: Kisha baada ya miaka mitatu nilipanda kwenda Yerusalemu ili kufahamiana na Kefa, nami nikakaa naye siku kumi na tano.
sw.B: Miaka mitatu baadaye ndipo nilipopanda kwenda Yerusalemu, ili kufahamiana na Kefa, nikakaa naye kwa siku kumi na tano.
sw.R: Miaka mitatu baadaye, nilipanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Nilienda kufahamiana na Petro, nikakaa naye kwa siku kumi na tano.

fr.L: Ensuite, après trois ans, je suis monté à Jérusalem pour faire la connaissance de Céphas, et je suis resté chez lui quinze jours.
fr.B: Trois ans plus tard, je suis bien monté à Jérusalem, pour faire la connaissance de Céphas, et je suis resté quinze jours auprès de lui.
fr.R: Trois ans après, je suis monté à Jérusalem. J’y suis allé pour faire la connaissance de Pierre, et je suis resté quinze jours avec lui.

ko.L: 그 후 삼 년 뒤에 나는 게바를 알려고 예루살렘으로 올라가서, 그와 함께 십오 일 동안 머물렀습니다.
ko.B: 그로부터 삼 년 뒤에야 나는 게바를 만나 알고자 예루살렘으로 올라가서, 그와 함께 보름 동안 머물렀습니다.
ko.R: 그로부터 삼 년이 지나서야 나는 예루살렘으로 올라갔습니다. 베드로를 만나 알고 싶어서 갔고, 그와 함께 보름 동안 머물렀습니다.

vi.L: Rồi sau ba năm, tôi lên Giê-ru-sa-lem để làm quen với Sê-pha, và ở với ông mười lăm ngày.
vi.B: Ba năm sau, tôi mới lên Giê-ru-sa-lem để làm quen với Sê-pha, và tôi ở với ông mười lăm ngày.
vi.R: Ba năm sau đó, tôi mới lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tôi đến để làm quen với Phi-e-rơ, và tôi ở với ông mười lăm ngày.

decisions.choice: after three years: counted most likely from Paul's call (verses 15-16)
alternatives: counted from his return to Damascus
decisions.reason: Ἔπειτα ("then") marks the next step in Paul's account, and the starting point is most naturally the event the account began with. Ancient counting often included the first and last years, so the time may have been a little over two years.

decisions.choice: to get to know Cephas: a visit to meet him and learn from him in person
alternatives: to be taught the gospel by him
decisions.reason: ἱστορέω was used of visiting a person or place in order to come to know it. It implies more than a courtesy call, but Paul's point (verses 11-12) is that this short visit, years after his call, was not where his gospel came from.

decisions.choice: Cephas: the apostle Peter
decisions.reason: Κηφᾶς is the Aramaic word for "rock", the name Jesus gave Simon (John 1:42). Peter is the Greek form of the same name, which Paul uses in 2:7-8.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Readable uses the name readers know (m3). Literal and Balanced keep the name Paul uses.

decisions.choice: "게바" (L, B); "베드로" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English and docs/corinthians-terms.md do: Literal and Balanced keep the Aramaic name Paul uses, in its Protestant Korean form "게바"; Readable says "베드로", the name readers know.

decisions.choice: "Sê-pha" (L, B); "Phi-e-rơ" (R); "ông" for him
decisions.reason: As in the English, Literal and Balanced keep the Aramaic name Paul uses, in the form of the Vietnamese John (1:42), and Readable gives the name readers know (m3). "Ông" is the respectful pronoun for a leading man of the church.

source.text: ἕτερον δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: Other but of the apostles not I saw, except James the brother of the Lord.

en.L: But I did not see another of the apostles, except James the brother of the Lord.
en.B: Apart from James, the Lord's brother, I did not see any of the other apostles.
en.R: I did not see any of the other apostles. The only one I saw was James, the brother of the Lord Jesus.

es.L: Pero no vi a otro de los apóstoles, excepto a Santiago, el hermano del Señor.
es.B: Aparte de Santiago, el hermano del Señor, no vi a ningún otro de los apóstoles.
es.R: No vi a ninguno de los otros apóstoles. El único al que vi fue Santiago, el hermano del Señor Jesús.

sw.L: Lakini sikumwona mwingine yeyote wa mitume, isipokuwa Yakobo ndugu wa Bwana.
sw.B: Isipokuwa Yakobo, ndugu yake Bwana, sikumwona mtume mwingine yeyote.
sw.R: Sikumwona mtume mwingine yeyote. Niliyemwona peke yake ni Yakobo, ndugu yake Bwana Yesu.

fr.L: Mais je n’ai vu aucun autre des apôtres, sinon Jacques, le frère du Seigneur.
fr.B: À part Jacques, le frère du Seigneur, je n’ai vu aucun des autres apôtres.
fr.R: Je n’ai vu aucun des autres apôtres. Le seul que j’ai vu, c’est Jacques, le frère du Seigneur Jésus.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 사도들 가운데 다른 사람은 보지 못했고, 주님의 형제 야고보만 [보았습니다].
ko.B: 주님의 형제 야고보 말고는 다른 사도를 아무도 만나지 못했습니다.
ko.R: 나는 다른 사도들은 아무도 만나지 않았습니다. 내가 만난 사람은 주 예수의 형제인 야고보뿐이었습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng tôi không gặp một sứ đồ nào khác, ngoại trừ Gia-cơ, anh em của Chúa.
vi.B: Ngoài Gia-cơ, anh em của Chúa, tôi không gặp một sứ đồ nào khác.
vi.R: Tôi không gặp một sứ đồ nào khác. Người duy nhất tôi gặp là Gia-cơ, em trai của Chúa Giê-xu.

decisions.choice: except James: James is counted among the apostles, in a wider sense than the Twelve
alternatives: I saw no other apostle, only James (who was not an apostle)
decisions.reason: εἰ μὴ can mean "except" (James is one of the apostles) or "but only" (James is outside the group). Paul lists James among those to whom the risen Jesus appeared, followed by "all the apostles" (1 Corinthians 15:7), and names him with Cephas and John as a pillar of the church (2:9).

decisions.choice: James the brother of the Lord: Jesus' brother, a leader of the church in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names a James among Jesus' brothers. This is not James the son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve, who was put to death early (Acts 12:2), but the James who led the Jerusalem church (2:9, 12; Acts 15:13). Christian traditions differ on whether these brothers were later sons of Mary or relatives in a wider sense; Paul's word is the ordinary word for brother.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus as the Lord meant.

decisions.choice: Santiago
decisions.reason: "Santiago" is the usual Spanish name for this James, the Lord's brother, and the name by which Spanish readers know the letter of James. "Jacobo" is used in some Bibles to keep the link with the patriarch Jacob.

decisions.choice: ndugu
decisions.reason: "Kaka" is specifically an older brother. "Ndugu" is the ordinary word for a brother and can also mean a near relative, so it leaves open the question the meaning decision mentions, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: Jacques
decisions.reason: "Jacques" is the usual French form of this name in the New Testament; "Jacob" is kept for the patriarch.

decisions.choice: "anh em của Chúa" (L, B); "em trai của Chúa Giê-xu" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether a brother is older or younger, which the Greek does not. Literal and Balanced keep the open "anh em", as the Vietnamese Mark does for Jesus' brothers (6:3). Jesus was Mary's firstborn (Luke 2:7), so Readable says "em trai", younger brother, as plain Vietnamese needs; a reviewer may prefer to keep "anh em" there too.

source.text: ἃ δὲ γράφω ὑμῖν, ἰδοὺ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.

records.literal_gloss: What but I write to you, look, before the God, that not I lie.

en.L: Now [in] what I am writing to you, look, before God, I am not lying.
en.B: Now, as God sees me, I am not lying in what I write to you.
en.R: God knows that what I am writing to you is true. I am not lying!

es.L: Y en lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, delante de Dios, no miento.
es.B: Delante de Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} aseguro que no miento en lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo.
es.R: Dios sabe que lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} escribo es verdad. ¡No estoy mintiendo!

sw.L: Basi [katika] mambo ninayowaandikia, tazama, mbele za Mungu, sisemi uongo.
sw.B: Basi, mbele za Mungu nawahakikishia kwamba sisemi uongo katika mambo ninayowaandikia.
sw.R: Mungu anajua kwamba mambo ninayowaandikia ni kweli. Sisemi uongo!

fr.L: Or ce que je vous écris, voici, devant Dieu, je ne mens pas.
fr.B: Devant Dieu, je vous l’assure : dans ce que je vous écris, je ne mens pas.
fr.R: Dieu sait que ce que je vous écris est vrai. Je ne mens pas !

ko.L: 보십시오, 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 것은 하나님 앞에서 [말하건대] 거짓말이 아닙니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서 보고 계시니, 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 이 말에는 거짓이 없습니다.
ko.R: 내가 여러분에게 쓰는 것이 사실이라는 것을 하나님께서 아십니다. 나는 거짓말을 하고 있지 않습니다!

vi.L: Về những điều tôi viết cho anh chị em, kìa, trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, tôi không nói dối.
vi.B: Trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời, tôi xin cam đoan rằng những điều tôi viết cho anh chị em không phải là lời dối trá.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời biết rằng những điều tôi viết cho anh chị em là thật. Tôi không nói dối!

decisions.choice: before God I am not lying: an oath calling God as witness
decisions.reason: Paul swears to the truth of his account in the same way in Romans 9:1 and 2 Corinthians 11:31. The sentence is incomplete in Greek ("look, before God, that I am not lying"): a verb such as "I declare" is understood before ὅτι.

decisions.choice: what I am writing to you: the account of Paul's movements in verses 15-19
decisions.reason: The oath stands in the middle of the account and backs up the facts just given, which the teachers in Galatia seem to have told differently.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: Modern English, as the style guide asks.

decisions.choice: as God sees me (B); God knows (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the call on God means instead of reproducing the exclamation.

decisions.choice: "kìa" (L) for "look"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the little word that draws the reader's attention; "kìa" is its current form, "nầy" the archaic one. Balanced and Readable say the oath in plain words (m1).

source.text: ἔπειτα ἦλθον εἰς τὰ κλίματα τῆς Συρίας καὶ τῆς Κιλικίας.

records.literal_gloss: Then I went into the regions of the Syria and of the Cilicia.

en.L: Then I went into the regions of Syria and of Cilicia.
en.B: After that I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
en.R: After that I went to the areas of Syria and Cilicia.

es.L: Después fui a las regiones de Siria y de Cilicia.
es.B: Después de eso fui a las regiones de Siria y Cilicia.
es.R: Después fui a las zonas de Siria y Cilicia.

sw.L: Kisha nilienda katika sehemu za Siria na za Kilikia.
sw.B: Baada ya hapo nilienda katika maeneo ya Siria na Kilikia.
sw.R: Baadaye nilienda sehemu za Siria na Kilikia.

fr.L: Ensuite je suis allé dans les régions de la Syrie et de la Cilicie.
fr.B: Après cela, je suis allé dans les régions de Syrie et de Cilicie.
fr.R: Après cela, je suis allé dans les régions de la Syrie et de la Cilicie.

ko.L: 그 후에 나는 시리아와 길리기아 지방으로 갔습니다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 나는 시리아와 길리기아 지방으로 갔습니다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 나는 시리아와 길리기아 지역으로 갔습니다.

vi.L: Sau đó, tôi đi đến các miền Sy-ri và Si-li-si.
vi.B: Sau đó tôi đi đến các miền Sy-ri và Si-li-si.
vi.R: Sau đó tôi đi đến các vùng Sy-ri và Si-li-si.

decisions.choice: Syria and Cilicia: the region around Antioch and, to its northwest, the coastland around Tarsus, Paul's home city
decisions.reason: Syria and Cilicia were joined in one Roman province at the time. Acts 9:30 says Paul was sent to Tarsus, and Acts 11:25-26 that he later worked in Antioch. Both are far from Judea, which is Paul's point (verse 22).

decisions.choice: areas
decisions.reason: A plainer word.

decisions.choice: Siria
decisions.reason: One Swahili name for Syria across the New Testament drafts: "Siria", the form Matthew 4:24, Mark 7:26, Luke 2:2 and 4:27 and Acts (14:26, 15:23, 15:41, 18:18, 20:3, 21:3) use. The older "Shamu" also names the Red Sea ("Bahari ya Shamu", Acts 7:36), which could confuse readers.

decisions.choice: "시리아", "길리기아"
decisions.reason: "시리아" is the current name, used in the Korean of Luke 2:2; "길리기아" is the established Protestant form.

source.text: ἤμην δὲ ἀγνοούμενος τῷ προσώπῳ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Ἰουδαίας ταῖς ἐν Χριστῷ, μόνον δὲ ἀκούοντες ἦσαν ὅτι Ὁ διώκων ἡμᾶς ποτε νῦν εὐαγγελίζεται τὴν πίστιν ἥν ποτε ἐπόρθει, καὶ ἐδόξαζον ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: I was but being-unknown by the face to the churches of the Judea the [ones] in Christ, \v 23 only but hearing they were that "The [one] persecuting us formerly now preaches the faith which formerly he was destroying," \v 24 and they were glorifying in me the God.

en.L: But I remained unknown by face to the churches of Judea that are in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; \v 23 they were only hearing, "The one who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith that he once tried to destroy," \v 24 and they glorified God because of me.
en.B: The churches of Judea that are in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} still did not know me by sight. \v 23 They only kept hearing it said, "The man who used to persecute us is now proclaiming the faith he once set out to destroy." \v 24 And because of me they glorified God.
en.R: At that time the churches in Judea that belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} had never met me. \v 23 All they knew was what others were saying: "The man who used to attack us is now telling others the good news, the very faith he once tried to wipe out!" \v 24 And they gave glory to God because of what had happened to me.

es.L: Pero yo seguía siendo desconocido de vista para las iglesias de Judea que [están] en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}; \v 23 solamente oían [decir]: «El que antes nos perseguía ahora anuncia la fe que antes trataba de destruir», \v 24 y glorificaban a Dios por causa de mí.
es.B: Las iglesias de Judea que están en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} todavía no me conocían en persona. \v 23 Solo oían decir una y otra vez: «El que antes nos perseguía ahora está anunciando la fe que en otro tiempo se propuso destruir». \v 24 Y glorificaban a Dios por causa de mí.
es.R: En ese tiempo, las iglesias de Judea que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} nunca me habían visto. \v 23 Solo sabían lo que otros decían: «¡El hombre que antes nos atacaba ahora anuncia la buena noticia, la misma fe que antes quería destruir!». \v 24 Y daban gloria a Dios por lo que había pasado conmigo.

sw.L: Nami nilikuwa sijulikani kwa uso na makanisa ya Yudea yaliyo katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; \v 23 ila yalikuwa yakisikia tu kwamba, "Yule aliyekuwa akitutesa zamani sasa anaihubiri imani aliyokuwa akijaribu kuiangamiza zamani," \v 24 nayo yalikuwa yakimtukuza Mungu kwa sababu yangu.
sw.B: Makanisa ya Yudea yaliyo katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} bado hayakunifahamu kwa sura. \v 23 Yalikuwa yakisikia tu watu wakisema, "Mtu yule aliyekuwa akitutesa sasa anaitangaza imani aliyokuwa ameazimia kuiangamiza." \v 24 Nayo yakamtukuza Mungu kwa sababu yangu.
sw.R: Wakati huo, makanisa ya Yudea yaliyo ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yalikuwa hayajawahi kukutana nami. \v 23 Waumini wa huko walijua tu yale ambayo watu wengine walikuwa wakisema: "Mtu yule aliyekuwa akitushambulia sasa anawaambia watu Habari Njema, imani ile ile aliyojaribu kuifuta kabisa!" \v 24 Nao wakampa Mungu utukufu kwa sababu ya yale yaliyotokea maishani mwangu.

fr.L: Mais j’étais inconnu de visage aux églises de Judée qui sont {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} ; \v 23 elles entendaient seulement dire : « Celui qui autrefois nous persécutait annonce maintenant la foi qu’il cherchait autrefois à détruire », \v 24 et elles glorifiaient Dieu à mon sujet.
fr.B: Les églises de Judée qui sont {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} ne me connaissaient toujours pas de vue. \v 23 Elles entendaient seulement répéter : « L’homme qui nous persécutait autrefois annonce maintenant la foi qu’il s’acharnait à détruire. » \v 24 Et elles glorifiaient Dieu à cause de moi.
fr.R: À cette époque, les églises de Judée qui appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ne m’avaient jamais rencontré. \v 23 Elles savaient seulement ce que disaient les autres : « L’homme qui nous attaquait autrefois annonce maintenant la bonne nouvelle, cette foi même qu’il essayait de faire disparaître ! » \v 24 Et elles rendaient gloire à Dieu à cause de ce qui m’était arrivé.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있는 유대의 교회들에게는 얼굴로는 알려지지 않은 채로 있었습니다. \v 23 그들은 다만 "전에 우리를 박해하던 사람이 이제는 그가 전에 없애려 하던 그 믿음을 전하고 있다" 하는 [말을] 듣고 있었을 뿐이며, \v 24 나 때문에 하나님께 영광을 돌렸습니다.
ko.B: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있는 유대의 교회들은 그때까지도 내 얼굴을 알지 못했습니다. \v 23 그들은 다만 "전에 우리를 박해하던 그 사람이, 이제는 자기가 없애려던 그 믿음을 전하고 있다" 하는 소문을 계속 들었을 뿐입니다. \v 24 그리고 나 때문에 하나님께 영광을 돌렸습니다.
ko.R: 그때 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 속한 유대 지방의 교회들은 나를 한 번도 만난 적이 없었습니다. \v 23 그들은 다른 사람들이 하는 말을 들어서 알고 있을 뿐이었습니다. "전에 우리를 공격하던 그 사람이 이제는 기쁜 소식을 전하고 있다! 자기가 없애 버리려고 했던 바로 그 믿음을 전하고 있다!" \v 24 그리고 그들은 나에게 일어난 일 때문에 하나님께 영광을 돌렸습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng các Hội Thánh ở Giu-đê, là những Hội Thánh trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, vẫn chưa biết mặt tôi; \v 23 họ chỉ nghe rằng: "Người trước kia bắt bớ chúng ta, nay đang rao giảng đức tin mà trước kia người ấy tìm cách hủy diệt," \v 24 và họ tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời vì tôi.
vi.B: Các Hội Thánh ở Giu-đê, là những Hội Thánh trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, vẫn chưa biết mặt tôi. \v 23 Họ chỉ nghe người ta nói: "Người trước kia bắt bớ chúng ta, nay đang rao giảng đức tin mà trước kia người ấy tìm cách hủy diệt." \v 24 Và họ tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời vì tôi.
vi.R: Lúc ấy các Hội Thánh ở Giu-đê thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} chưa từng gặp tôi. \v 23 Họ chỉ biết điều người khác nói: "Người trước kia tấn công chúng ta, nay lại đang nói cho người khác biết Tin Lành, chính là đức tin mà ngày trước người ấy tìm cách tiêu diệt!" \v 24 Và họ tôn vinh Đức Chúa Trời vì những gì đã xảy ra cho tôi.

decisions.choice: I remained unknown ... they kept hearing: a state that lasted through those years
decisions.reason: Both verbs are formed with εἰμί and a participle, which describes a continuing state: Paul stayed a stranger to them, and all they had was a report that kept reaching them.

decisions.choice: unknown by face to the churches of Judea: the believers in Judea had not met Paul in person
decisions.reason: τῷ προσώπῳ means "by sight". Judea here is the wider region; Paul had spent fifteen days in Jerusalem, mainly with Cephas (verses 18-19), and was not known to the congregations at large.

decisions.choice: in Christ: the Judean congregations that belong to Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase marks these as Christian churches, as distinct from the Jewish synagogues of Judea.

decisions.choice: the faith: the message believed, the gospel that calls for faith
alternatives: trust in Christ (the act of believing)
decisions.reason: Paul uses πίστις here for the content of what is believed, almost a name for the gospel itself, since it can be preached and attacked. Elsewhere in Galatians the word is usually the act of trusting (2:16).

decisions.choice: because of me: they praised God for what he had done in Paul
alternatives: in me (God was seen at work in Paul)
decisions.reason: ἐν ἐμοὶ gives the reason for the praise: the change in Paul, the persecutor turned preacher.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: is now preaching the faith (L); is now proclaiming the faith (B); is now telling others the good news, the very faith (R)
alternatives: preaches the gospel of the faith
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for proclaiming the gospel; its object here is "the faith" (m4), so Literal and Balanced use "preach" and "proclaim", and Readable keeps "tell the good news" and adds "the faith" beside it.

decisions.choice: had never met me
alternatives: were unknown to me by face
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: because of what had happened to me
decisions.reason: Readable says why they praised God (m5).

decisions.choice: Yudea
decisions.reason: Older Swahili Bibles call Judea "Uyahudi", but in verses 13-14 that word names Judaism, the Jewish way of life. "Yudea" keeps the region and the way of life apart.

decisions.choice: "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있는" (L, B); "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 속한" (R), for "in Christ" through the letter
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's phrase "in Christ", which Korean readers know; Readable says what it means here, the churches that belong to Christ, as the English Readable does. Where the phrase means being joined to Christ, Readable says "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 하나가 된".

decisions.choice: "믿음" for the faith at every level, Readable adding "기쁜 소식"
decisions.reason: "믿음" is the letter's word for faith at every level, as in Romans, and keeps the link with "믿다"; "신앙" means religious faith in general. Here it is the message believed (the meaning decision), so Readable names it as the good news, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" (L, B); "thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}" (R) for "in Christ" (for the whole letter)
alternatives: "ở trong Đấng Christ" at every level
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's phrase, which the reader can follow through the letter; Readable says what it means here, belonging to Christ (m3), as the Vietnamese Colossians does at Readable (1:2).

decisions.choice: "đức tin" for "the faith" at every level
decisions.reason: The faith here is the message believed (m4), but Vietnamese keeps the key term "đức tin" for pistis through the letter, so the reader can see the link with Paul's argument about faith in chapters 2-3.
